iriyāpathasamasīsī:
[Iriyāpatha+sama+sīsa+ī]  CL=10 An Arahant with avijja (ignorance) as the head, whose posture and cessation time are equal during meditation practice; and a person who attains Arahantship as soon as their posture changes during meditation practice, with the destruction of avijja.
(a) Among the four postures, one resolves: 'I will not change my posture and will strive to attain Arahantship.' While practicing vipassana with this determination, the attainment of Arahantship and the change of posture occur simultaneously. This person is called an Iriyapatha-samasisi.
(b) A person who practices vipassana in one of the four postures, becomes an Arahant, and attains parinibbana in that same posture is also called an Iriyapatha-samasisi.
